basis: set 2026-10-08 from runs on an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V laptop with an Arc 140V (WSL2, AC power), a little below the measured values; the measured value is in each comment

correctness._comment: bench/validate.py counts what pytest and GoogleTest report: 181 OpenCL pytest cases and 104 OpenCL GoogleTest cases at the time of writing

benchmark._comment: 1M x 384, k=10, inner product; qps is the median of three sweeps. Run-to-run spread was 7% at batch 1 and under 3.5% elsewhere, thermals added up to about 15%, so a regression has to cost 20% to fail

embeddings._comment: MiniLM on the GPU, 96 questions, support-rag's HNSW index. Measured: top-10 overlap FP16 1.000, INT8 0.975, INT4 0.792; mean cosine 1.0, 0.9992, 0.9664; source-in-top-10 drop vs FP32 0, 0, 0.035
embeddings._comment_ratios: measured INT4/FP16: peak RSS 1.22 (higher: weights are expanded at load), chunks/s 0.82 (slower: the model is too small for 4-bit weights to pay off on this GPU)

llm._comment: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct as support-rag's verifier on the GPU, 86 stored answers. There is no threshold on agreement with the original verifier: at every precision it is far below the 92% of always saying 'supported' (FP16 34%, INT8 45%, INT4 55%, kappa about 0), so it measures the model, not the quantization. The checks guard what quantization changes. Measured: agreement with FP16 INT8 0.86, INT4 0.63; kappa 0.03, 0.04, -0.05; decode INT4/FP16 2.4x; peak RSS 0.88; GPU allocation 0.32
